Euthanasia is best, if the pet is suffering. My first pet died naturally, but he was his usual old self right up to the morning I found him laying dead in the doorway. The second was euthanized when he could no longer walk. The vet came to the house and did it right there where the pet had chosen. The third - well, he was *at* the vet, but died of an enlarged heart we didn't know he had combined with the sedative to keep him calm enough for an x-ray. He HATED the vet. And he was so big they were afraid of him. I was an absolute mess when I had my other pet put down. He was 19, had looked horrible for the past year or so, but when he started leaking fecal matter I knew it was time. It's *possible* I could've had him treated, but I'd already decided I wouldn't put him through any more vet stuff aside from his yearly checkup. Poor pet was a nightmare at the vet, and as old as he was it just didn't seem fair to him. Even though I would've loved it if he'd lived forever.
